messages.content: Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response. Show a metric space (M, d) is complete if and only if any sequence (F_n) of nonempty closed subsets of M with - F_{n+1} \subset F_n - diam F_n \rightarrow 0 as n \rightarrow \infty has a nonempty intersection

message.content:
We prove both directions of the stated equivalence.
Does completeness imply the nested intersection property?
If M is complete and F_n is a nonempty closed decreasing sequence with diam F_n tending to zero, one can choose x_n in F_n for each n.
For n,m >= k, both x_n and x_m lie in F_k, so d(x_n,x_m) <= diam F_k, and the Cauchy criterion follows because diam F_k tends to zero.
Completeness then yields a limit x that lies in every closed F_n, so the intersection is nonempty.
Does the nested intersection property force every Cauchy sequence to converge?
Given a Cauchy sequence (x_n), the sets F_n defined as the closures of the tails consisting of all x_m with m >= n are nonempty, closed, nested, and their diameters tend to zero by the Cauchy condition.
Does the assumed property then provide a common point x of all the F_n?
The fact that x belongs to each closure of a tail and that the original sequence is Cauchy makes x the limit of (x_n), so M is complete and the two conditions are equivalent.

The statement: metric space complete iff any nested nonempty closed sets with diam ->0 has nonempty intersection. This is Cantor intersection theorem. Need prove both directions.

Direction 1: If complete, given F_n nonempty closed nested diam ->0. For each n choose x_n in F_n. Need show (x_n) Cauchy? Since x_n and x_m in F_k for n,m >= k? Actually F_n decreasing: if m>=k, x_m in F_m subset F_k; x_k in F_k. So d(x_n,x_m) <= diam F_k for n,m>=k (assuming k <= min? choose k <= n,m; if n,m >=k then both in F_k). Since diam F_k ->0, Cauchy. Complete -> x in M. Need x in intersection: for each n, x_{n+k} in F_n and F_n closed, limit x in F_n. Thus nonempty.

Direction 2: If property holds, prove M complete. Take Cauchy sequence (x_n). Need construct F_n = closure of tail {x_m : m >= n}. These are nonempty closed. Need nested: F_{n+1} subset F_n. Need diam F_n -> 0. Since x_n Cauchy, for epsilon choose N such that d(x_i,x_j)<epsilon for i,j>=N. Then closure of tail diam <= epsilon. More rigor: diam F_N = sup distances in closure tail; closure does not increase diameter? In metric space diam closure <= diam set? For any a,b in closure tail, choose points in tail close to a,b, triangle inequality gives < d(tail)+epsilon, sup <= diam tail. If tail Cauchy, diam tail ->0. Then property gives point x in intersection F_n. Need show x = lim x_n. For each epsilon choose N with d(x_i,x_j)<epsilon/2 for i>=N. x in F_N = closure tail, so there exists y in tail with d(x,y)<epsilon/2; choose i>=N y=x_i. Then for n>=N, d(x_n,x) <= d(x_n,y)+d(y,x) < epsilon. Limit. Hence complete.
